chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May Allah enhance you in righteousness! Whoever loves to meet Allah, does Allah also love to meet him? And whoever hates to meet Allah, does Allah also hate to meet him?' He replied, 'Yes.' I said, 'By Allah, I surely dislike death.' So he said, 'It does not mean what you think. It only applies at the time of viewing [what awaits a person after death]. Verily, when the believer sees what he loves, then there is nothing more beloved to him than proceeding [towards Allah], and Allah loves to meet him while he loves meeting Allah at that moment. And when he sees what he hates, then there is nothing more hateful to him than meeting Allah, the Almighty, and Allah [also] hates to meet him.'

And Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Yahya ibn Sabur said: 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The eye of the deceased weeps at the time of death.' He said, 'That is at the time of viewing the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), seeing what pleases him.' He said: 'Then he said: Do you not see the man when he sees what pleases him and what he dislikes, his eyes weep and he smiles?'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah love or hate meeting a person based on their view of death?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the general aversion to death and the specific spiritual state at the moment of 'mu'ayanah' (confrontation with the reality of the afterlife). It highlights that the believer's love for Allah is contingent upon witnessing the divine reward, while the disbeliever's hatred stems from confronting the divine punishment, a concept further supported by the companion's report on the deceased's emotional reaction upon seeing their destined fate. This underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the transformative power of direct vision (ru'ya) in determining the soul's ultimate affinity with the Divine.
